<reason>B wins through stronger comparative reasoning and more direct answers to pressure. A's Arizona account did not establish nationwide displacement sufficient to negate meaningful reduction, while B appropriately specified total unauthorized employment without inventing a percentage. B also explained how covert recruitment discrimination could be detected. Seasonal agriculture remained A's strongest objection and keeps the decision competitive, but B exposed the mistaken congressional-barrier claim and defended existing adjustment channels. A too often treated imperfect enforcement and costly adjustment as evidence that neither could meaningfully work.</reason>
<best_rebuttal>B's paired-application testing and agency-investigation answer directly defeated A's claim that an uninformed victim makes enforcement impossible. A's response that audits merely count victims did not answer their role in detection and punishment.</best_rebuttal>
